steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt, and baking soda together in a large bowl.
Beat sugar and butter together in a separate large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Add bananas, eggs, and vanilla; beat to combine.
Gradually blend in flour mixture until just combined; stir in chocolate chips.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls onto prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes. Transfer cookies to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These easy banana chocolate chip cookies are a scrumptious combination of mashed ripe bananas, semisweet chocolate chips, and vanilla.
raw_recipe.name: Banana Chocolate Chip Cookies

review.reviewBody: Very good recipe. I read the reviews first though and made the following changes - used only 1 teaspoon of baking powder and also split the 1 cup of white sugar to be 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar. I also used 1 1/2 cups of mashed bananas - 3 ripe bananas. These cookies were very moist, very cakelike and gone very quickly! Extra chocolate chips never hurt!

Okay recipe. Had to make a few adjustments based on other reviews, including using only 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 cup white sugar, and a little over 1/2 cup of the semisweet chocolate chips instead of the 2 cups it calls for. I added a 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts. I used three very ripe bananas and that came out to a little over 1 cup of mashed. I always substitute vegetable shortening for butter in every recipe, so that was a norm for me. I reduced the cooking temp to 350 and cooked them for about 13 minutes.

They turned out delicious!!!!!!! I am very happy with this cookie and will use this base + my alterations again and again, but I will probably lower the sugar amount just a tad next time and see how that turns out.

Just made these and they were pretty good. I read many reviews and made the following changes. 1/4 tsp baking powder, brown sugar instead of white, 1 egg, 1 cup of chopped nuts. I used a silpat on a dark cookie pan so I lowered the temp to 350 and cooked the full 12 min. I also flattened the dough before baking to make them less cake-like. Tried the first batch and thought it a little "flat", so mixed in some chunky peanut butter. They were much better. This makes a lot, I got 7 dozen using a small cookie scoop. I am sure my grandkids will love them.

I had 3 very ripe bananas , so I tried this recipe. My family loved them! Two changes I made though, I did turn down the oven temp to 350 degrees and used 1/2 white sugar and 1/2 brown sugar. You really do have to watch , because the tops stay very light, but the bottom gets brown quickly, so parchment paper works better for these. Also I did add 1 cup chopped pecans. Very soft cake like cookie.

I read previous reviews and did half cup white sugar and half cup brown sugar and lowered the baking powder to 1 teaspoon. I also made these into a bar cookie. I baked them at 350 degrees for 25 minutes and they were perfect.

These cookies are actually delicious, I decided to take my batch and put it into three parts, the first one I did just plain banana cookie, as my oldest boy doesn't like chocolate chips. The second batch I did with a healing huge tablespoon of peanut butter , And added peanut butter chipits . The third bowl was mixed in with chocolate chips as the recipe called for.

I turned my oven down because I found 400 was too hot as my oven cooks quickly, so I used it at 350°and cooked the cookies for 12 minutes.

They turned out perfect, the plane banana ones taste just like a slice of banana bread and the other ones are delicious as well. The peanut butter is perfect in them

First time making these. After reading several reviews, I decided to follow the recipe as is but omitted the chocolate chips. I baked them at 350° for 14 minutes and they came out perfect. Once cooled I add cream cheese frosting and they tasted like banana bread. I received several compliments. I will definitely make these again. These are cakey and not chewy, but oh so good!

Loved this recipe but I did make a some changes - 1 tsp Baking Powder instead of 2 , 1/2 cup butter instead of 2/3, 1/2 cup brown sugar & 1/2 cup white sugar instead of 1 cup white sugar, 2 Bananas, 2 cups chocolate chips instead of semi sweet, added- 1/2 cups pecans, & 1 tsp Cinnamon & Baked at 350* for 10-13 min. They are sooo delicious, just like a little piece of banana chocolate chip cakey heaven!!! YUM!!

Well, I gave this recipe 3 stars because I think it could have been better. When I made it, I adjusted some things, but the biggest thing that stood out in the original recipe was 400 degrees for 12-15 min -- I cannot see how this could not burn them to a crisp. I typically make regular choc chip cookies at 375 for 8 min., so I tried these the same way and they were perfect. I did make some other adjustments, though: I used 2 large bananas (about 1-1/2 c.), unsalted butter (but added 1 tsp. salt), I used 1 tsp. b. soda and 1 tsp. b. powder instead, and bumped the flour up to a full 3 cups. This made beautiful cake-like cookies. Perhaps the originals are more dense? I don't know, but I wanted a more cake-like cookie, and this worked perfectly.

Baked for 12 minutes at 400 degrees as recipe said. Did not burn at all, as some of the reviews state. I did add extra banana as I had 3 over ripe. And another 1/3 cup flour as I know my cookies tend to run thin for some reason. They held their shape. Didn't puff up much. I use a 2Tbs PC scoop. I do not grease as I use silicon baking liners. I have made this recipe many times and the grandchildren love them along with their Mommies.

Great recipe, just made a few tweaks! I just did 1/2 brown sugar and 1/2 white sugar, I used 2 ripe bananas. Cooked at 375 for around 10 minutes (I also chose to broil them for a couple minutes to brown the tops a little) They tasted awesome
I followed this recipe exactly and the cookies turned out perfect. Thick, soft, and just enough banana flavor. Thank you!

I used 2 very ripe bananas I would normally use in my banana bread but I would also add about 1/2 tsp Imitation banana flavoring. I only had 1 3/4 cups of Chocolate Chips but I think I would cut it even a little more to 1 1/4cups Choc. Chips. My oven is new so I'm still getting used to it, but I baked cookies at 400°F; I tried different times we found 14 minutes was perfect for my stove. Everything plays a part in making a recipe take on it's full flavours & take shape. It is all the tweaks that makes a gr8 recipe & it is what makes it yours!!

I was hoping to live this recipe because I love the pumpkin chocolate chip recipe… but I don’t. First, 400° is way too hot! I knew better but just went with it. Also, I should’ve gone through the reviews first to see people switching up the sugars. The flavor just wasn’t there for the original recipe, but maybe splitting granulated and brown sugars would have helped.

I didn’t read the directions and quite literally just put the oven to 350, put all the ingredients in (but with brown sugar not white and more bananas instead of butter) then put clumps of dough onto the pan and cooked for 17 minutes, yet they somehow came out so good NO ONE could stop eating them. Definitely recommend!!😎

Not impressed. Ended with a weird muffin like “cookie.” I followed the recipe exactly and the dough was weirdly sticky. I first baked one tray at 400 for 11 minutes, but at ~9 minutes I could smell them so I check them and they were burnt. I turned down the oven to 375, made them bigger (because honestly it was either going to be ok or be trash) and cooked them for 9 minutes. Definitely won’t be making these again.

Made this, however I mixed all the dry ingredients together and whisked it well. And mixed the butter alone unless fluffy, added the bananas and eggs, vanilla to it and mixed it well. Used 2 cups of dark and milk chocolate chips. Came out amazingly. 💖👏👏
Delicious, added a few more chips, and walnuts for half. They are great and will definitely make again. (Did not sift flour and they are still very fluffy.)

These cookies were good but not as good as regular chocolate chip cookies. Not as sweet. I did half brown sugar and half white sugar. I also added pecans . I set the oven to 375 degrees and baked 11 minutes.
I find these cookies have more the texture of muffins. Also didn't read the reviews and over cooked in 400 oven for 12 minutes. Probably won't make again.
